# Chapter 21 — sketch answers {.unnumbered}

\(1\) Spam filter: Machine learning (learns from labelled data, no deep network
implied). Chatbot: Generative AI --- an LLM producing text, the innermost box.
Expert system: AI but not machine learning --- hand-written rules, the 1980s
layer. Fraud model: Deep learning --- a neural network learning patterns, inside
ML, not generative. (2) The lure becomes a fluent, personalised email from a
one-letter-off supplier domain, followed by a deepfaked voice call from "the
supplier's accountant" pressing for a changed account number. Surviving
unchanged: The domain check, the pressure itself as a flag, the link/target
check --- and above all the process controls: Call back on the known number and
second-approve any payment change; the spelling heuristic dies, the out-of-band
verification does not, because it never depended on detecting the fake. (3)
Injection: A crafted customer message --- exploiting the model's inability to
separate instructions from data --- causes disclosure of other customers' order
data, harming confidentiality (R3-adjacent). Control: Least-privilege data
access for the bot plus output filtering; metric: Injection attempts detected in
red-team tests per quarter. Hallucination: The bot --- exploiting unverified
generation --- gives a customer wrong delivery or refund terms, creating
financial and trust harm. Control: Grounding answers in the order system plus
human escalation for commitments; metric: Sampled-answer error rate per month.
(4) (a) Minimal risk --- recommendation with no legal or similar effect; largely
unregulated. (b) High risk --- employment screening is a named high-risk use:
Strict obligations (and Chapter 9's fundamental-rights machinery) apply to
FastGoods as deployer. (c) Limited risk --- a chatbot carries transparency
duties, met by the disclosure already in the policy. (5) Sources: Expense and
card records filtered for AI vendors; SSO/network logs for AI domains. Question:
"Which AI tools actually help you, and what do you paste into them?" --- asked
blame-free, or the census measures silence. Conversion: Any tool receiving
personal, customer or confidential data gets a register row --- source (the
tool), event (data leaves control), consequence (GDPR/R3) --- plus either
onboarding as a proper supplier (Chapter 19) or a provided alternative; banning
without an alternative just re-hides the shadow.
